episodes.title: MDLW01 | Prof. Lenka Zdeborová | Insights on neural networks from statistical physics solvable models

screening.publisher_promise: Exactly solvable statistical-physics models of learning in neural networks (Isaac Newton Institute, Mathematics of Deep Learning workshop).
screening.screening_reason: A primary architect of the statistical mechanics of learning presents the programme: teacher–student models and replica/message-passing analyses that give exact learning curves. Competes with Wilson’s Bayesian account and Srebro’s implicit-bias account of why overparameterized models generalize. Rubric: A originator ✓ · B unifying principle ✓ · C derivation ✓ · D 2 (exact results, but only in high-dimensional limits) · E 2 · F 2 (exact solvability as a method).
screening.transcript_question: Which phenomena (double descent, benefit of depth, hardness of learning) are derived exactly, and which assumptions on data distribution make them solvable?
screening.caveat: Date and length not verified; title and channel verified by YouTube oEmbed.

episodes.title: A mathematical theory of learning in deep neural networks - Surya Ganguli

screening.publisher_promise: A mathematical theory of learning in deep networks (Initiative for the Theoretical Sciences).
screening.screening_reason: Ganguli, with Saxe, derived exact learning dynamics of deep linear networks and used them to explain stage-like semantic development. It derives representation formation from the dynamics rather than from an objective, which the repo’s compression-based anchors (Ma, Wilson) do not. Rubric: A originator ✓ · B unifying principle ✓ · C derivation ✓ · D 1 (linear-network idealization) · E 2 · F 2.
screening.transcript_question: What do the exact deep-linear dynamics predict about the order in which structure is learned, and which predictions survive nonlinearity?

episodes.title: What is learning? Singularities and pendulums — Daniel Murfet

screening.publisher_promise: An introduction to singular learning theory from the metauni SLT seminar; the seminar lists a transcript.
screening.screening_reason: Singular learning theory (Watanabe; developed for deep learning by Murfet’s group) says that neural networks are singular statistical models, so classical asymptotics fail and the geometry of degenerate minima (the learning coefficient) governs generalization. It is a direct, mathematically specific rival to flatness and parameter-count explanations. Rubric: A originator ✓ · B unifying principle ✓ · C derivation ✓ · D 2 (contested empirical relevance at scale) · E 2 · F 2 (learning coefficient as complexity).
screening.transcript_question: How is the real log canonical threshold defined and estimated, and what does it predict that flatness or PAC-Bayes do not?
screening.caveat: Seminar page lists the date in day-month-year form and a transcript; length not verified.

screening.publisher_promise: Salam Distinguished Lecture at the International Centre for Theoretical Physics.
screening.screening_reason: Bialek is the originator, with Nemenman and Tishby, of predictive information: the information the past carries about the future as the quantity organisms and learners should extract. screening.transcript_question: Does the lecture derive predictive information and its optimal-extraction principle, or stay at the level of examples?

episodes.title: Engineering and Reverse-Engineering Intelligence Using Probabilistic Programs, Program Induction, and Deep Learning

screening.publisher_promise: NIPS 2017 tutorial by Josh Tenenbaum and Vikash Mansinghka on probabilistic programs, inference programming and program induction.
screening.screening_reason: The originators of the probabilistic-programming account of intelligence: common sense as inference in structured generative programs (intuitive physics and psychology as game-engine-like models). It is the strongest competing account to purely statistical learning in modules 4 and 6, and the repo has no Tenenbaum. Rubric: A originator ✓ · B unifying principle ✓ · C derivation ✓ · D 2 (scaling critique from deep learning) · E 2 · F 2.
screening.transcript_question: Which inferences need structured programs rather than amortized networks, and what do they gain in sample efficiency and generalization?

episodes.title: Mathematical Mysteries of Deep Neural Networks — Stéphane Mallat (2019 Lytle Lecture)

screening.publisher_promise: University of Washington Lytle Lecture on what regularity deep networks exploit.
screening.screening_reason: Mallat built wavelet scattering: invariance and stability to deformations, obtained by iterating wavelet transforms and modulus, are derived as what a convolutional network must compute. It gives module 2 a constructive mathematical answer about priors, competing with learned-prior accounts. Rubric: A originator ✓ · B unifying principle ✓ · C derivation ✓ · D 2 (scattering versus learned features) · E 2 · F 2.
screening.transcript_question: What does scattering explain about CNNs, and where do learned networks exceed it (and why)?
screening.caveat: Video embedded on the UW ECE page (posted 18 Dec 2019); length and language not shown, presumably English.
